instruction: I went on a dinner with some of my coworkers yesterday. I paid the entire bill to simplify the payment. I've made a note of individual shares in simple note. Some people have already sent me their share on venmo. Make payment requests for others with a description note "Work Dinner".
notes: The real coworker set, their shares and who already paid are only known at runtime, so the problem uses placeholder coworkers: coworker-1 (already sent a 'Work Dinner' venmo transaction, no request) and coworker-2/coworker-3 (pending, need requests). World facts that lookups reveal (coworker-email from phone.search_contacts, share from simple_note.show_note, already-paid from venmo.show_transactions) are static in :init but gated by nullary knowledge predicates (coworkers-found, shares-known, transactions-checked) that only the corresponding lookup actions make true, forcing the plan to perform every information-gathering call. Because supervisor-complete-task must have the ground goal conjunction as its precondition, the goal entities (coworker-2, coworker-3, their share amounts and the 'Work Dinner' description) are declared as domain constants rather than problem objects. token-of is a naming device that pins each placeholder token to its app so bindings stay unambiguous. venmo.show_transactions is modeled with direction='received' and min_created_at=yesterday; sort_by is omitted as non-essential. phone.get_current_date_and_time supplies 'yesterday' used both to pick the note and to filter transactions. No answer is passed to complete_task; the evaluation only checks the added PaymentRequest records (receiver, amount) match the pending coworkers' shares.
